one_month_reasoning: No Micron earnings in the window (FQ1 FY27 report expected mid/late Dec 2026). In-window events: Samsung Q3 preliminary (~8 Oct) and full results (~end Oct), SK hynix Q3 results (late Oct), hyperscaler Q3 prints with first 2027 capex colour (late Oct), monthly DRAM contract-price data (end Oct). Peers should confirm tight supply, so those are mildly supportive, but the stock's reaction to a ~7-8% guide beat was only +0.9% over two sessions, which suggests positioning is full and peak-cycle worry caps upside; any hint of capex deceleration (UBS sees +25% in 2027 vs +76% in 2026) would hit memory hardest. No strong post-earnings drift signal. I therefore use a near-symmetric lognormal centred slightly below spot (~$1,068) with ~20% one-month sigma (realized 80%/3.5 ~ 23%, trimmed slightly since part of the realized vol came from the 5x run-up).

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of (a) FY28 EPS $185 (10% below $206 consensus) x 5.5x peak-cycle P/E = $1,018 and (b) a cycle-aware discounted FCF to Oct-2027 (FY28-31 FCF/share $140/$75/$32/$25, terminal $55 mid-cycle EPS x 12, 11% discount) of $669 plus ~$174/share net cash = $843. Blend ~$930.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $205.95 haircut ~10%: management guides 'more moderate' price increases through FY27 and opex +$2.5B [2]; HBM demand-destruction risk as GPU makers shift 12-high to 8-high [23,24]; Korean capacity (SK hynix Y1 Feb-27, Samsung P5 1H27) lands in FY28 [17]; hyperscaler capex growth slowing to +25%/+6% in 2027/28 per UBS [20].

Peer median fwd P/E 5.1x (range 4.2x-23.7x); memory-chip makers (SK hynix, Samsung, Kioxia, Nanya, Winbond) 4.2x-4.9x; MU historically trades mid-single-digit P/E at earnings peaks [25]. Small premium to memory core for SCA price floors (~35% of revenue to 2030, $150B RPO) and $68B net cash [2], which are contractual and persist through the horizon; kept inside the peer range.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Value at Oct-27 = PV(FCF/share FY28 $140, FY29 $75, FY30 $32, FY31 $25) + PV(terminal: $55 mid-cycle EPS x 12 = $660) at 11% = $669; plus net cash ~$174/share

inputs_detail.derivation: $185 EPS + ~$12 D&A - ~$57 capex/share (~$65B FY28 capex: FY27 >$50B implied by $25B in 1H and higher 2H, with construction capex growing meaningfully faster [2]); ~1.15B shares [2]. = ~$140.

Downturn as new cleanrooms (Micron ID1/ID2/Japan, Samsung P5, SK hynix Y1, CXMT 420-500k wpm) come on line in 2028; Morningstar expects steep pricing decline 2029-31 [7]; Burry cites 34 drawdowns >30% and FCF negative in 48% of quarters historically [6]; capex cut to $35-40B in the trough.

Mid-cycle EPS ~$55 (~$63B net income, far above FY25 $8.29 [1]) assumes structurally higher HBM/data-center mix and SCA floors [2]; 12x mid-cycle P/E consistent with trading mid-single-digit at peaks and higher at mid-cycle [25].
High-beta cyclical (80% realized vol per brief, deep historical drawdowns [6]); equity cost ~11% with negligible debt [5].

inputs_detail.input: Net cash per share at Oct-27
inputs_detail.derivation: Net cash $68.3B less $12.7B returnable SCA deposits [1,2] = $55.6B, plus ~$145B FY27 FCF (consensus FY27 EPS $176.42 [3] x 1.15B sh + D&A - >$50B capex [2]); ~$200B / 1.15B shares; buybacks treated as value-neutral.

bear.story: By mid-2027 the market looks through the shortage: contract-price increases stall as Korean fabs, Micron ID1/Tongluo and CXMT ramp, hyperscaler capex growth decelerates (UBS +25% in 2027, +6% in 2028), and HBM content per GPU falls (8-high stacks). FY28 consensus is cut toward $130 and the stock is priced at a 4-4.5x trough-anticipating multiple plus cash. Consistent with MU's history of 50-70% peak-cycle drawdowns.

base.story: FY27 delivers roughly consensus ($170-180 EPS) and FY28 ~$185-200, but investors treat 2027-28 as the earnings peak; the multiple compresses to ~5-5.5x FY28 while cash piles up. Stock roughly flat to slightly down.

bull.story: Shortage proves structural (management sees no line of sight to balance; SK hynix CEO sees demand above supply past 2030), HBM 2027 resets +50-140%, FY28 EPS $230+ and the market pays 7-8x for SCA-backed earnings.

comps_summary.peer_range: Fwd P/E 4.2x (Winbond) to 23.7x (Seagate); memory-chip makers 4.2x-5.3x, storage/controller names 8x-24x. EV/EBITDA figures are TTM (forward not published on the source), range 7.0x-43.4x, median 13.7x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 5.5x FY28 EPS: slightly above the 5.1x peer median and above the 4.2x-4.9x memory-chip core, well below the HDD/controller names. MU itself trades 6.1x FY27.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Only a small premium to the memory core is granted, for contractual features that persist through the horizon: SCAs with price floors covering >35% of revenue to 2030 and ~$150B RPO, plus $68B net cash [2]. No premium to the storage/controller names: MU's capital intensity (>$50B FY27 capex) and commodity DRAM exposure make it more cyclical, and Moody's own upgrade notes SCA prices are capped [9], limiting upside capture.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$600 (-44%) the market would be capitalising FY28 EPS of roughly $110 at a peak multiple, i.e. pricing an outright DRAM/HBM price decline in 2027 or SCA renegotiation, not just multiple compression. At that level I would conclude the cycle has turned earlier than the 2028-29 timing in my base case (bearish thesis confirmed and a base-case thesis broken).

reasoning: Starting facts: FQ4 FY26 revenue $54.2B, non-GAAP EPS $33.42, FQ1 guide $61.5B/$38.15 (~8% above LSEG), net cash $68.3B, $12.7B customer deposits [1,2]. Consensus FY27/FY28 EPS $176/$206 puts MU at 6.1x/5.2x [3,5]. Skeptic evidence: (1) Supply is coming: SK hynix Y1 (Feb-27) and Samsung P5 (1H27), Korea doubling memory capacity, CXMT to 420-500k wpm and ~11% bit share by 2028 [17,18,19]; Micron's own FY27 capex >$50B with ID1/Tongluo output mid-2027 [2]. (2) Demand risk: UBS sees hyperscaler capex growth falling from +76% to +25% and +6% [20]; TrendForce warns of HBM demand destruction and 8-high stacks [23,24]; Nvidia HBM price-hike coverage names only SK hynix and Samsung [22]. (3) Smart-money/sell-side caution: Burry short disclosed at ~$1,052 [6]; Morningstar cut FV to $700 and expects a 2029-31 pricing slump [7]; Erste downgrade on capex [8]; PT range low $361 [4]. (4) Insiders: ~$91M sold in 90 days, $0 bought; CEO selling steadily under a Jan-26 10b5-1 plan [10-14] - weak signal given plan, but no buying. (5) Credit is not a risk: Moody's upgrade, $5.2B debt [1,9]; short interest only 2.5% [5]. (6) Litigation is a tail: Netlist ITC exclusion request, prior $445M willful verdict [15,16]. Weighing honestly: near-term fundamentals are extremely strong and supply-constrained through 2027 per management [2], so a collapse within 12 months needs an early turn; but stocks discount the cycle 12-18 months ahead and Oct-2027 is when the 2028 supply wave is visible. The Polymarket AI-bubble market (Dec-26) traded ~16-28% Yes in search snippets (volume not retrievable, page 503) [21] - treated as sentiment only. Fair value ~$930 (blend of $1,018 P/E and $843 cycle-aware DCF). Scenarios: bear $560 (32%), base $1,020 (45%), bull $1,700 (23%); expected ~$1,030, median ~$1,000, slightly below spot. Ladder is a three-lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.35/0.25/0.25), giving P(>=1075) 0.42, consistent with 80% realized vol and fat left tail typical of memory peaks. Research limits: Twelve Data insider/target endpoints and Alpha Vantage were plan/rate-limited; Seeking Alpha and some pages returned 403; forward EV/EBITDA for peers unavailable, TTM used.
